audit_findings.title: Cash-settled convertible principal makes the share denominator incoherent
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately 7.06 million excess shares at the $92.06 valuation-date price; correcting them would raise bull value from $61.92 to approximately $66.99 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The full approximately 9.25 million-share conversion ratio appears in fully diluted shares even though the $650 million principal must be cash-settled; only approximately 2.19 million premium shares would be issuable at $92.06, while retained interest expense is consistent with continued debt treatment.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion of the Convertible Notes, the Company must satisfy the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The mandatory cash-principal settlement is demonstrated, although the denominator's exact composition still requires reconciliation. Using the supplied figures, removing approximately 7.06 million excess shares reduces the denominator from 93.323 million to approximately 86.26 million and increases scenario values by about 8.2%. Even the corrected bull value of approximately $66.99 remains about 27% below the $92.06 market price, so this cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every component of the 93.323 million-share ceiling, replace full conversion shares with premium shares under the contractual settlement method, and rerun per-share values while retaining note interest unless conversion and debt extinguishment are explicitly assumed.

audit_findings.title: Growth may omit the working-capital reinvestment required to produce it
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 working-capital and other cash use of $802.4 million, versus $402.2 million generated in FY2025; $1,204.6 million year-over-year swing
audit_findings.mechanism: If working-capital movements were excluded from owner earnings without a normalized replacement charge, projected OE and the terminal value grow without funding the additional receivables and inventory required for sales growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash used for working capital and other was $802.4 million during fiscal 2026, compared with cash generated from working capital of $402.2 million in fiscal 2025, primarily reflecting higher inventory purchases, the timing of payments for inventory purchases and higher accounts receivable due to increased sales and cash collection timing.
audit_findings.explanation: An omission has not been demonstrated because the OE schedule showing normalization was not supplied. The possibility is nevertheless material: the filed FY2026 working-capital use was more than twice the $358.4 million OE anchor, and the business states that growth normally consumes working capital. Even a fraction of the reported use, if recurring, could materially reduce the $42.54-$61.92 per-share valuation range.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE construction and build a normalized incremental-working-capital requirement from receivables, inventory, payables, factoring and receivable-sale data; apply it separately to each growth scenario and rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: A pre-valuation term loan is absent from the earnings basis
audit_findings.magnitude: $375 million principal; net annual OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The loan's post-tax interest expense reduces forward equity-level OE, while any operating income, debt refinancing benefit or interest income produced by its proceeds may offset that burden.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 12, 2026, subsequent to the end of fiscal 2026, the Company entered into a credit agreement (“2026 Term Loan”) for $ 375 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The borrowing before the valuation date and its absence from FY2026 earnings are demonstrated. Materiality cannot be established from the record because the outstanding balance at September 5, use of proceeds, applicable spread, contemporaneous SOFR and incremental income are not supplied. The $375 million principal equals approximately 104.6% of anchor OE, but principal itself is not the valuation adjustment under the stated equity-OE method.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the valuation-date balance, borrowing rate and use of proceeds; calculate the post-tax incremental interest burden net of income or financing costs displaced, then rerun forward OE and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The cash addition may include required operating cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum identified bridge overstatement of $155.396 million, or approximately $1.67 per share; $146.4 million was held outside the United States
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding operating, restricted or economically inaccessible cash to the equity bridge double-counts an asset required to support the OE-producing business.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash balances held outside the United States that cannot be remitted in a tax-efficient manner are generally used to support local working capital requirements, including inventory purchases, capital expenditures and other foreign business needs.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether any particular cash balance is surplus remains unresolved. However, the effect is bounded by the entire $155.396 million addition: removing all cash would lower bull value from $61.92 to approximately $60.25 per share, still about 35% below the $92.06 market price. Thus even the maximum identified adjustment cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash and freely transferable, tax-efficient surplus cash by jurisdiction, then replace the bridge addition with only verified surplus cash for valuation precision.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved legal and regulatory claims remain unbounded
audit_findings.magnitude: Excess exposure unquantified; $6.2 million of probable and estimable compliance liabilities was recorded at June 27, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Losses beyond existing accruals would reduce future OE or constitute claims against equity not captured in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For certain of these matters, it is not possible to determine the ultimate outcome, and the Company cannot reasonably estimate the maximum potential exposure or the range of possible loss, particularly regarding matters in early stages.
audit_findings.explanation: No additional loss is demonstrated or reasonably estimable. The filing records $6.2 million for probable and estimable matters, states that other exposure cannot be bounded, and expects no material effect on financial position or liquidity, although a single period could be affected. This is therefore a forward-looking contingency to monitor rather than a presently supportable valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Monitor subsequent filings, legal-counsel updates, settlements, insurance and indemnification coverage; open a quantified bridge or OE adjustment only when a loss amount or probability range becomes supportable.
